items.rationale: The model keeps nothing between sessions; memory is a store the program writes to and loads from. Choosing a (window too small) or c (forgetting over time) treats the model as if it remembered by itself.
Each call re-sends the whole transcript, so the fixed 2,000 tokens are sent on all 3 calls: 3 x 2,000 = 6,000. An answer of 2,000 treats the model as remembering earlier calls.
Tool results enter the window and are re-sent on every later call, so returning only the needed day shrinks every later call. A larger window gives room, not savings.

items.answer: It searches stored chunks of the manual for those closest in meaning to the question and puts only the top few matching chunks into the window.
accepted: It searches the manual and puts only the best-matching chunks into the window
A search tool finds the most relevant chunks and returns only those
The manual is split into chunks and the closest matches to the question are retrieved
items.rationale: Retrieval is a search over text outside the window that brings in only the top-k best matches. An answer saying the model recalls the page from training is wrong.

items.answer: Bookings go stale, so a weeks-old note may be wrong; the assistant should call the calendar tool, which is current.
accepted: The note is out of date; check the calendar tool instead
Bookings change, so notes should hold lasting facts only and the calendar should be queried
It may be stale, so call check_calendar for the current bookings
items.rationale: Notes are claims from the past, so they suit lasting facts like training status. For things a tool knows and that change, such as bookings, call the tool. A good answer names staleness and the tool.
